cards.title: CONCEPT
cards.text: Sixth concept. One-to-one replication of the Arctic Goddess claymation diorama (FB 858092580487604, 38 days running): every element sculpted from warm tan terracotta clay with visible fingerprints, including the headline itself as thick rounded clay lowercase letters, with the product jar as the only real object in frame. Their scene ran a clay vacuum sucking at a clay bloated belly. Ours runs a sculpted clay stomach with a clay wind-up key being turned in its side, the honest visual for motility restarting. Three headline variations, identical diorama, all closing on IN WEEKS. 4:5 at 1080x1350. REVISED 2026-08-26: close changed from IN 5 DAYS to IN WEEKS after Brooks flagged five days as overpromising.

cards.title: OURS · three headlines, one diorama  ·  ours

cards.text: NOTES

cards.title: WHY 'IN WEEKS' AND NOT A NUMBER
cards.text:
Brooks, 2026-08-26: 'Five days is overpromising.'

He is right, and the distinction is worth holding onto. Day five is what the mechanism bible supports for the FIRST normal, non-cramping movement. It is not when the thing is fixed. The bible's own words for the full arc are 'fills in over a few weeks' and 'rewards consistency, not a one-bottle test.'

Putting 5 DAYS on the creative quietly promised the finished result on the first-movement timeline. IN WEEKS promises the actual outcome on the actual timeline, and it puts us back on the reference's exact close.

The body copy still names day five, because in context it is correctly hedged and correctly scoped: it says the first movement usually lands around then, not that everything is resolved. That is the honest version and it stays.

cards.title: SAME ISSUE LIVE IN MOT-XRAY-CELERY-01
cards.text:
That concept's three headlines all read CELERY = ... IN 5 DAYS, and CLEARED OUT IN 5 DAYS is a harder promise than anything on these clay ads.

The same reasoning applies: day five is the first-movement marker, not the finished result.

NOT CHANGED YET, because those three headlines were picked by name (3, 5 and B from a list of ten) and swapping the close to IN WEEKS changes their punch. Brooks's call. It is one batch of three re-renders whenever he wants it.

cards.title: THE VISUAL TRANSLATION
cards.text:
The reference's engine is simple: an appliance is physically doing something to a body part. A vacuum with a hose attached to a belly. That is the beat to port, not the vacuum itself.

Ours: a large sculpted clay stomach, the classic curved J shape with inlet and outlet tubes, standing on the table. Set into its side is a clay wind-up key, and a clay hand is turning it. Small clay motion arcs curl around the key.

A wind-up key is the cleanest possible visual for restarting something that has stopped moving, which is literally what motility is. It also carries the honest version of the mechanism: nothing is sucked out or forced through, the thing is simply started again. A vacuum would have implied a laxative.

THE STOMACH HAS NO FACE, no eyes and no mouth. Deliberate. The house law against personifying objects still applies, and a cartoon face would cheapen a scene that currently reads as craft.

The clay alarm clock reinforces waking up without spending a word of copy on it.

cards.title: REVISION LOG
cards.text:
Pass 1: single ad. Jar slightly right of centre, second headline line clipped at the right edge, celery rendered pale green rather than clay.

Pass 2: three headlines. Jar centred, margins fixed, celery pulled into tan clay.

Pass 3 (current): close changed from IN 5 DAYS to IN WEEKS.

CENTRING: state the composition rule BEFORE describing any object, and place every prop RELATIVE TO THE JAR rather than by absolute corner. That is what holds it.

MARGINS: the one-fifth rule, and name the radiating dashes explicitly. A margin instruction about letters does not cover the decorative marks beside them, which is exactly what got cut.

NUMERALS: when removing a number from sculpted lettering, add an explicit line saying there are no numbers anywhere in the clay lettering. Otherwise the model tends to reinstate the digit it saw in the prior composition.

cards.title: WHY THE CLAY STAYS TAN
cards.text:
The reference is monochrome tan and the bottle is the only colour in it.

Keeping the clay tan means the green Motilli jar is the single saturated object in an otherwise warm neutral frame, which is exactly the mechanic the reference uses with its purple bottle. Rendering the clay in Motilli green would flatten that contrast and lose the product.

Different call from MOT-GUTRESET-01, where the ask was explicitly to use Motilli's colours, because that layout is a flat graphic with no such contrast to protect.

cards.title: PRIMARY TEXT · all three
cards.text:
Your colon is a muscle. Muscles do not move unless something tells them to.

A GLP-1 slows digestion down, which is the whole point and it works. The trouble is the slowdown reaches all the way to your colon, and the signal that tells that muscle to contract starts to fade.

That signal is a short-chain fatty acid called butyrate, and you do not make it yourself. The bacteria in your colon make it out of the fiber that reaches them. Slow everything down and less reaches them. The colony thins out, butyrate falls, the muscle gets a weaker instruction, and less moves the next day. It feeds on itself, and the medication holds that first slowdown in place, which is what keeps the loop shut.

Motilli is built to start it again rather than force anything through. Concentrated celery juice standardized for a real dose of apigenin, which barely absorbs into your bloodstream and so stays down in the colon where the problem is, calming the lining and shifting the balance back toward the butyrate makers. Plus a fine soluble prebiotic fiber to feed those bacteria once they come back.

Rebuild the place, then feed what grows there.

The first few days are quiet, because this is not a laxative and nothing is being forced. The first normal, non-cramping movement usually lands around day five. It fills in from there.

None of it touches your weight loss. Weight loss lives in the brain and the appetite. This lives in the colon. Two separate systems, so you rebuild one and stay on the other.

Two gummies before bed with a full glass of water. Sixty in a bottle. Third-party tested, lab results posted.

Ninety days to decide. Email inside ninety days and every dollar comes back, no return required.

cards.title: FRAME QA · all three, current version
cards.text:
Close: PASS. 'in weeks' with a clay dash either side, fully inside the frame in all three. No digits anywhere in the clay lettering.

Jar centring: PASS. Dead centre in all three, stomach left, alarm clock right, balanced.

Headline margins: PASS. Both lines and the radiating clay dashes sit fully inside the frame with clear clay wall on both sides.

Clay lettering: PASS. Spelled exactly. GLP-1 rendered correctly in H1 including the hyphen and numeral, which is the one place a numeral belongs.

Stomach: PASS. Correct J shape with inlet and outlet, wind-up key set into the side, clay hand turning it, motion arcs present. No face in any of the three.

Monochrome: PASS. Every prop including the celery stalks is tan clay. The jar is the only real and only coloured object.

Jar: PASS. motilli wordmark and CELERY JUICE FIBER GUMMIES legible in all three.

No invented words, badges, prices or percentages.

cards.title: AUDIT
cards.text:
Law 2: no invented study, percentage, doctor, review count or customer quote. The creative now promises only 'in weeks', which matches the bible's own framing of the full arc.

Law 9: all three headlines cleared lawgate. No em dashes, no negation-affirmation beats, no parallel stacks. No personification: the clay stomach has no face.

Two separate systems: present in the body copy.

Swap test: PASS. The butyrate loop, apigenin staying in the colon, and the rebuild-then-feed order are ours. The wind-up key visual argues against laxatives without naming one.

Shelf life: evergreen.

CLAIM RISK: low, and lower than before the change. No body imagery, no before and after, no numeric timeline on the creative.

VERIFY BEFORE LAUNCH: the 90-day no-return-required guarantee wording against the live policy page.
